R068-01.notes: P2 (silence frames sounds concertgoers were trained to ignore) and the final paragraph (change in attention) support C. A contradicts 'Cage insisted that they had not been' victims of a joke. B reverses the passage's view. D is an unsupported 'first ever' claim. Facts checked: the premiere was 29 Aug 1952 at the Maverick Concert Hall, Woodstock; Tudor marked the movements with the keyboard lid and a stopwatch; Cage gave the wind, rain and audience-talking account himself. All accurate.

R068-02.notes: Stated directly in P1. D (the stopwatch) is a fair trap because the stopwatch is mentioned in the same sentence.

R068-03.notes: In P2, the third movement's sounds are 'the audience itself, talking and walking out', and the silence 'frame[s] these sounds'. A treats the piece as silent, which Cage denies. B and C have no support.

flags.note: 'A few years earlier' is loose: Cage's Harvard anechoic chamber visit is usually dated 1951, one year before the premiere, although Cage's own accounts varied. 'Shortly before' or 'not long before' would be safer. This does not affect any answer.

R068-04.notes: The paragraph opens 'Cage had come to this view partly through an experience', which signals B. A is too narrow, since the chamber is only defined in passing. C and D belong to other paragraphs. The engineer's explanation (nervous system and blood circulation) matches Cage's own account and is properly attributed to the engineer.

R068-05.notes: 'his own nervous system and his own blood in circulation' means his own body. The paraphrase is accurate.

R068-06.notes: It follows from the chamber anecdote, where even in the quietest room he heard his own body. B contradicts the passage. C is a misreading, because the chamber did absorb outside sound. D is off-topic.

R068-07.notes: View 1 is 'a philosophical statement more than a musical work, an idea'. View 2 is 'a genuine composition'. 'Lasting' is a reasonable paraphrase, set against 'loses its force once it has been understood'. A, B and C are not discussed.

R068-08.notes: 'Both views, perhaps, miss the piece's quietest achievement ... listening differently afterward.' The answer hedges ('suggests'), which matches the author's 'perhaps'. A contradicts the passage. C and D have no support.

R068-09.notes: Here 'frame' means to set off or present these sounds so they are noticed. B (the literal meaning) is the intended trap. C is the 'frame someone' meaning. D is 'frame a question'. Only A fits.

R068-10.notes: At five minutes, rereaders 'remembered slightly more', so a researcher who tested only then would wrongly conclude that rereading is better. B is the true one-week finding, which that researcher could not have observed. C comes from Ebbinghaus and is not a mistaken conclusion. D reverses the confidence finding, since rereaders were more confident. Facts checked against Roediger and Karpicke (2006): restudy beat recall at 5 minutes, recall beat restudy after 1 week, and restudy groups predicted better recall. Ebbinghaus tested intervals of up to about a month, with a steep loss in the first day. All accurate.
